title: Cerulean Security - Private VPC Discovery
topics: Private control plane and data residency
Latency/cost tradeoffs hosted vs dedicated vs private
summary: Initial discovery for Private/VPC deployment for Cerulean Security. Main concerns: network architecture (VPC peering vs Private Endpoints), regional availability, KMS integration and compliance. Next steps: send security pack, schedule technical deep dive and internal network diagram, share pilot pricing and baseline benchmark guide.
next_steps: Samira to send Redwood security pack (SOC2, ISO27001, network diagrams) - by 2026-10-20
Ethan to schedule technical deep dive focused on VPC networking and peering options - proposed 2026-10-19
Customer to share internal network diagram and list of acceptable IP ranges/regions - by 2026-10-18
Agree pilot scope and benchmark tests for latency/throughput - next meeting
action_items: Samira Khan: Send security and compliance docs (SOC2, ISO) and sample SLA language - due 2026-10-20
Ethan Cole: Prepare VPC peering vs Private Endpoint config guide and sample IaC snippets - due 2026-10-19
Miguel Torres: Share VPC CIDR ranges, existing transit gateway details, and preferred regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) - due 2026-10-18
Liam O'Connor: Provide list of security controls required for KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention needs - due 2026-10-18
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intro, Ethan's our solutions engineer. Could we do quick 1-line intros?
[00:08] Aisha Patel: Sure. Aisha, Head of Infrastructure at Cerulean. We're evaluating options for hosting an LLM inference platform, need private VPC deployments.
[00:15] Miguel Torres: Miguel, Platform Eng, I'll handle the networking bits.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Liam, Security, focusing on KMS and compliance.
[00:21] Ethan Cole: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to understand your network constraints, regional requirements, and how you'd like Redwood to connect — VPC peering, private endpoints, or a transit model.
[00:32] Aisha: Yeah, we're mostly AWS today, some GCP in other teams but primary is AWS. We need everything in our VPCs, no public endpoints.
[00:40] Samira: Understood. Do you have any existing transit gateway / peering pattern?
[00:44] Miguel: We use a central transit gw — sorry, "transit gateway" uh, TGW — across accounts, so peering into that is preferred. We also have strict IP ranges and want control over egress.
[00:53] Ethan: Cool, that's common. Redwood Private supports a few options: VPC peering to a dedicated Redwood VPC in the same region, PrivateLink-style private endpoints (we call them private endpoints), or a customer-managed peering into a dedicated cluster. For TGW we can attach via a VGW/TGW attachment pattern too.
[01:10] Liam: For security, KMS integration is mandatory. All model data in transit and at rest must use our CMK. Do you support bring-your-own-key?
[01:18] Ethan: Yes, BYOK via customer KMS is supported. We have integrations with AWS KMS and support HSM-backed keys for on-prem HSMs in Private deployments; docs will show key policy examples.
[01:29] Miguel: A few questions on network egress — if we peer, do tokens leave our VPC at any time? What's the data plane flow?
[01:36] Samira: Good call, we should clarify. Ethan, can you walk the flow?
[01:40] Ethan: Sure. For the dedicated Private deployment, inference traffic stays on the private link between your VPC and Redwood's compute subnets; there is no public internet hop for model traffic. Model artifacts can be pulled during deploys via a secured channel; if you want absolute control we can arrange air-gapped on-prem option or ensure artifact fetches go through your S3 with restricted roles.
[01:58] Aisha: Artifact fetch via our S3 and role-based access would be ideal. We need audit logs for all pulls.
[02:05] Ethan: Audit logs are configurable — we push detailed request logs to a customer-owned CloudWatch or S3 bucket and also keep an internal audit trail. We can surface logs in the Redwood Console and forward to your SIEM.
[02:16] Liam: Retention? For some workloads we need 7 years — that's a lot.
[02:20] Samira: Long retention is an add-on; we'll include retention tiers in the security pack.
[02:24] Miguel: Region-wise, we're constrained to EU data residency for a handful of clients. Which regions do you support for Private?
[02:30] Ethan: We have Private deployments in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 in-preview; eu-west-1 is GA for Private, eu-central-1 is scheduled for GA in Q4. APAC is coming through partners. We'll clarify exact availability in the pack.
[02:43] Aisha: How about cross-region failover? We need DR., we can't have live traffic cross outside EU for primary workloads.
[02:50] Ethan: We support same-region primary with cross-region replication options for model artifacts. For live traffic you'd keep it within EU regions; cross-region only for failover and it's configurable per-route.
[03:00] Miguel: Ok. On peering, do you support transitive routing? Our TGW handles transit, we don't want complex static routes.
[03:07] Ethan: For TGW, we can integrate via TGW attachments so traffic can route transitively through your central networking stack. That avoids per-account peering.
[03:15] Miguel: Nice. What about private endpoints — are they PrivateLink? We have strict policy allowing only AWS endpoints of certain service names.
[03:21] Ethan: They are AWS PrivateLink-style endpoints. We can provide service names that your security team can allow. There's also a VPC peering option if you prefer that model. Note that PrivateLink gives you fine-grained endpoint control and avoids route table changes.
[03:34] Rina Chaudhry: Sorry I joined late, procurement question — pricing for Private and any minimum commitment?
[03:38] Samira: We have a Dedicated/Private pricing model typically with reserved capacity for Dedicated, and Private has a mix of platform fee plus infra usage. We'll send an initial quote and pilot pricing, no long-term commit required to start a limited pilot.
[03:50] Miguel: Latency — we need p50 under 50ms for short text inference. Is that realistic in a private peered setup?
[03:56] Ethan: Yes, with co-located compute in the same AZ or region and continuous batching tuned to your latency SLO we can meet p50 under 50ms for typical small models. Heavier models or long sequences change that; we'll propose a benchmark plan.
[04:10] Aisha: About RBAC and SSO — we use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. Can you integrate?
[04:16] Samira: Yes, SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning is supported; RBAC is configurable on per-team and per-route basis.
[04:23] Liam: Audit and compliance again — do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? Also pen test reports?
[04:28] Ethan: We are SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certified. We'll include the attestations and a recent pen test summary in the security pack, and offer an NDA to share full reports if needed.
[04:39] Miguel: A few more nitty-gritty: do you allow IP allowlists and static egress IPs for callbacks/webhooks? We use some third-party integrations that need fixed IPs.
[04:48] Ethan: We can provide static egress IP ranges for Private clusters. For hosted public API that varies, but in Private deployments we can reserve elastic NATs and provide the ranges to you.
[04:58] Aisha: Networking notes: our infra folks want terraform snippets.
[05:02] Samira: Ethan will prepare sample IaC with TGW/TGW attachments and PrivateLink examples.
[05:08] Miguel: On the model side, are you maintaining models or do we bring our own? We want to run some fine-tuned models privately and also use Redwood-curated open models for other workloads.
[05:16] Ethan: Both. We support customer model registry and pinned versions; you can host artifacts in your S3 and we can fetch via a role. For Redwood-curated models we offer validated variants and quantization profiles. For private customer models we recommend pinning and running canaries to ensure performance and cost.
[05:30] Liam: Data retention in logs and possibility to redact PII — can we configure per-route redaction?
[05:36] Ethan: Yes, per-route data handling policies and redact rules can be configured; we also support on-the-fly obfuscation and client-side preprocessing before tokens hit the service.
[05:45] Aisha: Who will own the network changes on our side? We'll likely have an internal task to approve service names and route tables.
[05:51] Miguel: We'll own that, but need a clear checklist from Redwood.
[05:55] Samira: We'll provide a Network Integration Checklist and sample runbook for your ops team.
[06:00] Rina: Procurement also needs contract SLAs around uptime and incident response for Private.
[06:05] Samira: We'll include SLA language. For Dedicated/Private we offer SLA-backed uptime tiers and priority support.
[06:12] Miguel: A question about model caching and KV cache — can the KV cache be kept in our VPC? We want cache warmers to be inside our network.
[06:20] Ethan: The KV cache is normally co-located with the compute nodes; for Private deployments we can attach a customer-managed cache or ensure the KV cache doesn't leave the VPC. We'll detail options in the tech deep dive.
[06:33] Liam: Any compliance pitfalls for EU customers when using telemetry?
[06:36] Ethan: Telemetry is configurable — we can disable telemetry or route telemetry through your collector. We'll note GDPR considerations in the pack.
[06:43] Aisha: Timeline: we need a pilot within 6 weeks ideally. Is that feasible?
[06:48] Samira: Yes, a restricted pilot with 2-4 nodes in eu-west-1 is doable in 4-6 weeks once we have network access and sign basic contracts.
[06:57] Miguel: Ok good. On-call and escalation: who do we contact during pilot incidents?
[07:01] Samira: You get a CSM + access to our incident channel; for Dedicated/Private pilots we assign a SE and on-call rotation. We'll include contacts in the next email.
[07:10] Ethan: I'll prepare the Tech Deep Dive doc with diagrams: VPC peering, PrivateLink endpoint names, TGW attachment examples, sample IAM roles for S3 artifact fetch, and KMS policy examples.
[07:21] Miguel: Also include route table examples for the TGW model and the exact subnet requirements.
[07:26] Samira: Great. Any other blockers we should know?
[07:29] Liam: Main one for security is access to KMS keys and strict audit trail. Procurement will need pricing.
[07:34] Rina: We'll need to review pricing with legal but pilot pricing first.
[07:38] Samira: Perfect. Quick recap and owners: I'll send security pack and pricing, Ethan will send network IaC + tech deep dive, Miguel/Liam to share network diagram and KMS requirements. Can we aim to reconvene next Tuesday Oct 19th for the tech deep dive?
[07:52] Aisha: Works for us.
[07:53] Miguel: Yep.
[07:54] Liam: Fine.
[07:55] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite.
[07:59] Rina: Thanks.
[08:01] [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains minor mishears; some product names abbreviated. Shared artifact references: "security pack (link to docs)", "tech deep dive deck (link)" and "pilot pricing spreadsheet (link)" are mentioned and will be attached in follow-up email.
